races.title: State House, District 86
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Hugh Blackwell
cands.bio: Republican attorney and partner in a Valdese law practice, with a Harvard Law degree. He has served in the North Carolina House, District 86 (part of Burke County), since 2009. He previously served on the Burke County School Board.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Blackwell was born or raised, or when he came to North Carolina. The pages we had show no deeds or stated positions on data centers, homestead property taxes, land buying by investors or foreigners, growth and land protection, immigration or H-1B, police pay, guns, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. The list of bills he sponsored was empty on the page we read. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey, and no endorsements were listed for 2026. No controversies turned up. The dates of his school board service were not given.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Attorney and law-firm partner (Harvard Law graduate) in Valdese. Member of the NC House since 2009, and earlier a Burke County School Board member.
qual.why: He has about 17 years of prior legislative service plus a law career, which fits the high band for writing law and the state budget. Committee chair posts were not counted toward the score.

cands.name: Wesley E. Hendrix
cands.bio: Democratic candidate for the North Carolina House of Representatives, District 86, in 2026. He advanced without a primary and lost the general election to incumbent Hugh Blackwell (R). No other background is available in the sources reviewed.

endorsements.text: Listed on Ballotpedia as recommended by the voter guide groups NC Public School Champions and Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy, both Sway voting groups.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Wesley Hendrix was born or raised, when he came to North Carolina, or his occupation and work history. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey, and no campaign website, interview or questionnaire was available, so we found no stated positions on data centers, development, property taxes, immigration, guns, abortion, education or policing. We found no record of any office he has held and no documented controversies.
